verses.text: Yahweh says, “Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool. What kind of house will you build to me? Where will I rest?
For my hand has made all these things, and so all these things came to be,” says Yahweh: “but to this man will I look, even to he who is poor and of a contrite spirit, and who trembles at my word.

He who kills an ox is as he who kills a man; he who sacrifices a lamb, as he who breaks a dog’s neck; he who offers an offering, as he who offers pig’s blood; he who burns frankincense, as he who blesses an idol. Yes, they have chosen their own ways, and their soul delights in their abominations:

I also will choose their delusions, and will bring their fears on them; because when I called, no one answered; when I spoke, they didn’t listen; but they did that which was evil in my eyes, and chose that in which I didn’t delight.”

Hear Yahweh’s word, you who tremble at his word: “Your brothers who hate you, who cast you out for my name’s sake, have said, ‘Let Yahweh be glorified, that we may see your joy;’ but it is those who shall be disappointed.
A voice of tumult from the city, a voice from the temple, a voice of Yahweh that repays his enemies what they deserve.
“Before she travailed, she gave birth. Before her pain came, she delivered a son.
Who has heard of such a thing? Who has seen such things? Shall a land be born in one day? Shall a nation be born at once? For as soon as Zion travailed, she gave birth to her children.
Shall I bring to the birth, and not cause to be delivered?” says Yahweh. “Shall I who cause to give birth shut the womb?” says your God.
“Rejoice with Jerusalem, and be glad for her, all you who love her. Rejoice for joy with her, all you who mourn over her;
that you may nurse and be satisfied at the comforting breasts; that you may drink deeply, and be delighted with the abundance of her glory.”

For Yahweh says, “Behold, I will extend peace to her like a river, and the glory of the nations like an overflowing stream; and you will nurse. You will be carried on her side, and will be dandled on her knees.
As one whom his mother comforts, so will I comfort you. You will be comforted in Jerusalem.”
You will see it, and your heart shall rejoice, and your bones will flourish like the tender grass. Yahweh’s hand will be known among his servants; and he will have indignation against his enemies.
For, behold, Yahweh will come with fire, and his chariots will be like the whirlwind; to render his anger with fierceness, and his rebuke with flames of fire.
For Yahweh will execute judgment by fire and by his sword on all flesh; and those slain by Yahweh will be many.

“Those who sanctify themselves and purify themselves to go to the gardens, behind one in the middle, eating pig’s meat, abominable things, and the mouse, they shall come to an end together,” says Yahweh.
“For I know their works and their thoughts. The time comes that I will gather all nations and languages, and they will come, and will see my glory.

“I will set a sign among them, and I will send those who escape of them to the nations, to Tarshish, Pul, and Lud, who draw the bow, to Tubal and Javan, to far-away islands, who have not heard my fame, nor have seen my glory; and they shall declare my glory among the nations.

They shall bring all your brothers out of all the nations for an offering to Yahweh, on horses, in chariots, in litters, on mules, and on camels, to my holy mountain Jerusalem, says Yahweh, as the children of Israel bring their offering in a clean vessel into Yahweh’s house.
Of them I will also select priests and Levites,” says Yahweh.
“For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me,” says Yahweh, “so your offspring  and your name shall remain.
It shall happen that from one new moon to another, and from one Sabbath to another, all flesh will come to worship before me,” says Yahweh.
“They will go out, and look at the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me; for their worm will not die, nor will their fire be quenched, and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”

footnotes.content: Heaven His throne, earth His footstool—yet He asks where we'll build Him a house. There's something tender in the question, like a grandfather asking about a gift you're struggling to give. God isn't searching for a place to live; He's searching for our honest hearts.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: "To this man will I look"—the Lord's gaze rests on the poor, the contrite, the one who trembles at His word. Not the proud builder or the confident, but the one who knows their own smallness and holds Scripture with reverent fear. This is where His attention goes.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: To kill an ox for God or kill a man are one to Him when the heart is wrong. Even the grandest offering, the sweetest incense, becomes an abomination when divorced from a right spirit. God sees through the temple's outward show to the soul's actual state.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When we've refused to hear His voice, He Himself becomes the echo of our own choices—reaping what we've sown. There's a quiet judgment here: we choose our delusions, then find ourselves alone with them. The Lord steps back and lets our own way teach us.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Your own brothers cast you out for bearing His name, then speak of glorifying Him while longing for you to fail. The irony stings—but hold fast. Those who mock the faithful will themselves be disappointed; God's eye is on the faithful remnant, not the crowd.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A voice from the city, a voice from the temple—the Lord's judgment reaches into both the streets and the sanctuary. He renders to His enemies their due. This is the sound of righteousness coming full circle.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Before the travail, the child—a wonder that defies the natural order. Zion will birth her children in a moment, swift and sure, without the pain that usually attends birth. This is grace irrupting into the expected way of things.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A whole nation born in a day—who has heard of such a thing? Yet this is what the Lord promises for Zion. The impossible becomes routine under His hand. When He acts, the world's timescales shatter.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He who opens the womb doesn't close it. The God who brings to birth will see delivery through. There's a certainty here, a covenant assurance: what He begins, He completes. We may doubt, but He does not.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Rejoice with Jerusalem, all you who love her; rejoice with joy, all you who mourn over her. There's a gracious invitation here—to join in her vindication, to trade mourning for celebration. To love Zion is to hope with her.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Nurse at her breasts, drink deeply of her abundance. The image shifts from watching to feeding, from hope to sustenance. Jerusalem becomes a mother herself, pouring out nourishment and delight to all who belong to her. The comfort flows outward.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Peace extending like a river, nations' glory flowing like a flood—the Lord promises abundance so real you can taste it, so constant you can rest in it. Like a child carried on the hip and dandled on the knee, His people are held close and cherished.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As a mother comforts, so will I comfort you. The Lord speaks in the idiom of human tenderness—He knows the ache of homesickness, the power of a mother's arms. In Jerusalem, you will be comforted. You will know you are held.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When you see it, your heart rejoices and your bones flourish like grass—not a metaphor, but a real bodily relief, a tangible restoration. God's care reaches down to the smallest places. And His indignation falls on those who oppose His people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whirlwind chariot, fire, the rebuke of flames—His coming is terrible and righteous. Don't mistake the long patience of God for indifference. When He comes in judgment, all history bends to His purpose.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Fire and sword execute His judgment on all flesh; those slain by the Lord will be many. The text doesn't soften this. God's holiness is not negotiable, and His judgment falls where pride and rebellion stand.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Those who sanctify themselves behind one in the gardens, eating forbidden things—the scene speaks of religious pretense cloaking disobedience. They end together, their false holiness crumbling. The Lord knows a counterfeit when He sees one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord knows their works and their thoughts—nothing is hidden from Him. And the time comes when He gathers all nations and languages to see His glory. The whole earth will witness. What is hidden now will be made known then.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He sets a sign among them and sends survivors to far-away islands—Tarshish, Pul, Lud, Tubal, Javan. The Gospel reaches the ends of the earth, carried by those who have seen His glory. No place is too distant for His fame to travel.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All your brothers brought as an offering to the Lord—on horses and chariots, in litters and on camels, from all nations. The scattered are gathered, the distant brought near, all as an offering of reconciliation. The whole world streams to His holy mountain.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From among the nations, He selects priests and Levites. The privilege of serving Him is no longer confined to one tribe; the whole redeemed family becomes His ministers. Access to the holy is opened to all who believe.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: As the new heavens and new earth remain before Me, so shall your offspring and name remain. Your children, your legacy—they endure in the eternal order. What you are, what you believe, ripples forever in God's new creation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From one new moon to another, from one Sabbath to another, all flesh comes to worship. The rhythm of worship never ceases in the age to come. Every rhythm, every season points toward Him. Eternity is not silence; it is unending praise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They will look at the dead bodies of transgressors—worm not dying, fire not quenching. Readers today hear an echo of final judgment, the consequence of rejecting Him made manifest. Yet even this stern close leaves room for grace: the choice to turn is still ours, as of now.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
